title: What is open enrollment?
summary: Explains what open enrollment is, the enrollment dates for ACA, employer, Medicare, Medicaid and D-SNP coverage, and what to do if you miss the deadline.

atoms.title: What open enrollment means
atoms.question: What is open enrollment?
atoms.text: An open enrollment period is a window of time that happens once a year, typically in the fall, when you can sign up for health insurance, adjust your current plan or cancel your plan. It is usually limited to a few weeks. If you miss it, you may have to wait until the next open enrollment period to make any changes.

atoms.title: Which insurance types have open enrollment
atoms.question: What types of insurance use open enrollment?
atoms.text: People who get health insurance through a job, through Medicare or through the Affordable Care Act (ACA) marketplace have an open enrollment period. Medicaid programs, including the Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP), have no open enrollment period.

Which health plans have an open enrollment period?

atoms.title: Open enrollment dates by coverage type
atoms.question: What are the open enrollment dates for each type of coverage?
atoms.text: ACA Marketplace plans for individuals and families: open enrollment is November 1 through January 15 in most states. Health insurance through work: enrollment periods are set by the employer, typically in the fall. Medicare: the Annual Enrollment Period (AEP) is October 15 to December 7 every year, and the Initial Enrollment Period (IEP) is around age 65. Medicaid and Dual Eligible Special Needs Plans (D-SNP): enroll anytime.

atoms.title: When ACA open enrollment happens
atoms.question: When is open enrollment for ACA plans?
atoms.text: For UnitedHealthcare Individual & Family ACA Marketplace plans, open enrollment for most states is November 1 through January 15. Some state-based markets may have open enrollment periods that differ from federal-based marketplaces, as well as special enrollment periods.

atoms.title: Open enrollment for job-based coverage
atoms.question: When is open enrollment if I get health insurance through my work?
atoms.text: If you get health insurance through work, your employer sets the open enrollment period. It is typically in the fall so that your benefits can start at the beginning of the calendar year. Choosing a health care plan for the year ahead is an important decision, so take time to explore your options before you enroll.

atoms.title: When Medicare enrollment happens
atoms.question: When is Medicare enrollment?
atoms.text: One key Medicare enrollment period for changing coverage is the Annual Enrollment Period (AEP), which runs from October 15 to December 7 every year. During AEP you can join, switch or drop a plan. If you make no changes during AEP, your current plan will automatically renew the next year. The Initial Enrollment Period (IEP) is around age 65.

atoms.title: Open enrollment for Medicaid
atoms.question: Is there an open enrollment period for Medicaid?
atoms.text: There is no open enrollment period for Medicaid programs, including the Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP). In all states Medicaid provides coverage to low-income families and children, pregnant women, the elderly and people with disabilities, and some states cover all low-income adults below a certain income level. To apply, contact your state agency that manages the Medicaid program.

atoms.title: Open enrollment for Dual Special Needs Plans
atoms.question: When is open enrollment for a Dual Eligible Special Needs Plan?
atoms.text: People who have both Medicaid and Medicare benefits could be eligible for a Dual Special Needs Plan (D-SNP). Those who qualify for this type of Medicare Advantage plan can switch to a new plan at any point during the year, not just during open enrollment.

atoms.title: Changes outside open enrollment
atoms.question: Can I make changes outside of the open enrollment period?
atoms.text: Typically, once you have made your benefit elections, you have to wait until the next open enrollment period to make changes. Not always, though. Qualifying life events are life events that let you make changes to your benefits outside of the open enrollment period.

atoms.title: What to do if you missed open enrollment
atoms.question: What if I missed the deadline for open enrollment?
atoms.text: If you need coverage when annual open enrollment is not available and you have not had a qualifying life event, you can buy short term health insurance or a fixed benefit health plan. Short term health insurance can fill needs for 1 month to nearly 1 year, depending on your state. TriTerm Medical can provide coverage for up to 3 years in select states. Fixed benefit plans pay preset amounts for qualified medical services and are a supplement to health insurance, not a substitute for ACA minimum essential coverage.

atoms.title: Questions to ask before choosing a plan
atoms.question: What should I think about before choosing a health insurance plan?
atoms.text: Before choosing a plan during open enrollment, consider four questions. How much did you spend on health care last year, including your premium, deductible and out-of-pocket costs? Did what you or your family spent line up with your health care needs? Is your doctor or clinic in network? Are your medications covered?
